title: Charred Tofu Salad
subtitle: with Broccoli, Radish and Lime
description: If you're looking for good-for-you food, then here's your ticket. There's protein-rich satay tofu, a good dose of calcium from the greens, plus brain-boosting peanuts – and flavour in spades!

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Bring a medium saucepan of water to the boil for the broccoli. Trim the broccoli, then cut into long florets. Finely grate the zest of half the lime, then juice the half. Cut the remaining lime into wedges. Thinly slice the radish. Cut the tofu into 2cm-thick strips.
Cook broccoli: Cook the broccoli in the pan of boiling water for 2-3 mins until tender. Drain, then cool under cold running water.
Make dressing: Put the lime zest, juice, 1 tbs vegetable oil, 1 tbs soy sauce and 2 tsp honey in a large bowl, season with pepper and stir to combine.
Char tofu: Heat 1 tbs vegetable oil in a small frypan over high heat. Cook the tofu for 1-2 mins each side until warmed through and slightly charred.

Serve up: Add the broccoli, radish and salad leaves to the dressing and toss to combine. Coarsely chop the peanuts. Divide the salad among bowls, top with the tofu, then scatter over the peanuts. Serve with the lime wedges for squeezing over. Enjoy!

Did you know?: Peanuts aren't actually nuts, they’re legumes (like lentils and peas), and they're very good for you. Yes, they’re high in kilojoules (so don’t stuff yourself with them) and rich in fat, but it’s unsaturated fat, which helps lower bad cholesterol. Peanuts are a great source of protein and antioxidants, plus they help boost brain power too.
